```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(dsOMOPClient)
```

The QueryLibrary integration distinguishes an upstream clinical question from
its published SQL. The SQL is training/reference material and is never executed
by the sticky redesign path. Instead, a typed recipe or plan defines the
population and variables, the server prepares a person-local `omop.table`
sealed for DP, and a pinned mapping fixes one of the seven sticky primitives
and its longitudinal reducer.

The roles are those of DataSHIELD: the analyst chooses the question (the
population, the derived variables such as an age at a public reference year,
and the public bins or levels); the data custodian owns every privacy setting
(whether DP is available, epsilon, caps and the community tools' protection
mode). No client argument changes those.

## Automatic questions (dsOMOP 2.9.0)

The common person-level questions need no preparation at all. With the
server's default `dsomop.tools.mode = "auto"`, the analysis catalog answers the
per-person durations and counts (for example `condition.duration_stats`,
`drug.days_supply_stats`, `condition_era.eras_per_person_stats`) with a
histogram of one value per person over fixed public bins, and the demographic
distributions (`person.year_of_birth_distribution`,
`person.gender_by_age_decade`) with a complete public partition, both with
sticky DP noise of sensitivity one person. A server whose DP service is not
available answers the same table under the standard DataSHIELD controls.
Every result says how it was protected:

```{r automatic, eval=FALSE}
res <- ds.omop.analysis.run("dsomop:condition.duration_stats",
                            params = list(concept_id = 201820))
res$pooled             # persons per duration bin, summed across servers
res$meta$protection    # per server: "dp" (epsilon, noise SD) or a fallback
```

Questions with an automatic equivalent list it in
`omop_querylibrary_sticky_catalog()$automatic_equivalent` and when printed.

## Sticky redesigns

The core never uses differential privacy (dsOMOP 2.8.0 and later): tables
loaded with `ds.omop.plan.execute()` or `recipe_execute()` carry no DP
provenance, and the server refuses them as DP inputs. A sticky redesign is
released on a table prepared for DP from a typed recipe or plan
(`ds.omop.dp.prepare()`, dsOMOP 2.9.1 or later). The release prepares it for
you when the redesign carries its recipe.

This is deliberately not a QueryLibrary SQL runner or an arbitrary join/query
gateway. An upstream ID selects only a reviewed semantic mapping; it neither
submits the upstream SQL nor constructs a data-dependent query. Preparation and
release remain two explicit, typed steps.

The client cannot choose epsilon, seed, nonce, privacy epoch or rerolls. Actual
releases default to the server-owned contract reported by
`ds.omop.dp.status()`: `sticky_person_bounded_discrete_laplace_per_release_v1`
under `fixed_per_release_snapshot_first_answer_v1` (server 2.7.1, client
2.7.4). It permanently retains one complete first answer per public request,
snapshot and epoch, even after any size of unrotated source update. Custodian
rotation restores freshness; new requests need not represent the same source
version as previously answered requests. Person-level contribution bounds and
first-release calibration are unchanged. Public new identities reserve storage;
existing identities remain readable at capacity. There is no lifetime privacy
budget or privacy call quota. Legacy v2 services remain inspectable and are
refused for release by default. During site-by-site upgrades,
`options(dsomop.dp.allow_legacy_servers = TRUE)` permits legacy and mixed v2/v3
releases, including through `ds.omop.querylibrary.sticky.release()`. Every
legacy server produces a warning: no first-answer binding: an unrotated data
refresh can reveal whether a released statistic changed; see
isglobal-brge/dsOMOP#20. First-answer replay applies only to the v3 sites.
Results retain each site's protocol and contract in
`meta$privacy$per_site_contract`, identify `legacy_servers` and
`mixed_contracts`, and retain warnings in `meta$warnings`, even for pooled-only
output. Shared contract fields that differ across sites are `NULL`. Return
the option to its default `FALSE` after the federation upgrades.

```{r catalog}
catalog <- omop_querylibrary_sticky_catalog()
table(catalog$statistic)
```

Every category domain, numeric/date break, bound, concept set, time window,
ordering rule and record cap must be public and fixed before data access.
Observed categories and data-dependent top-N selection are not valid inputs.

For example, PE12 can be redesigned as a coarse age-at-a-fixed-public-year
distribution. This avoids placing exact birth components in the prepared table
and uses public decade breaks:

```{r birth-year}
age_at_2025 <- omop_querylibrary_sticky(
  "PE12",
  variable = "age_at_2025",
  breaks = seq(0, 120, by = 10)
)
age_at_2025
```

Give the redesign its recipe and release it in one call; the input is
prepared on every server, released, and removed:

```{r execute, eval=FALSE}
recipe <- omop_recipe(
  variables = omop_variable_age(name = "age_at_2025", year = 2025),
  outputs = omop_output(name = "ages", type = "wide")
)
age_at_2025 <- omop_querylibrary_sticky(
  "PE12", variable = "age_at_2025", breaks = seq(0, 120, by = 10),
  preparation = recipe
)
result <- ds.omop.querylibrary.sticky.release(age_at_2025, datasources = conns)
```

The same step can be explicit, for example to release several statistics on
one prepared table:

```{r prepare, eval=FALSE}
ds.omop.dp.prepare(recipe, out = c(ages = "DP_ages"))
result <- ds.omop.querylibrary.sticky.release("DP_ages", age_at_2025,
                                              datasources = conns)
```

The whole release population must be defined in the recipe or plan: filtering,
merging or otherwise manipulating a prepared table drops its DP provenance.
Variables whose protection depends on other persons cannot be prepared; for
example a baseline `age_at_index` (protected with cross-person age banding) is
refused in favour of an age at a public reference year.

Longitudinal numeric and categorical record histograms use a deterministic
declared order and a finite per-person record cap:

```{r records}
monthly_conditions <- omop_querylibrary_sticky(
  "CO19",
  variable = "month_number",
  breaks = seq(0.5, 12.5, by = 1),
  max_contributions = 12,
  order_by = "month_number"
)
```

Scalar record totals and site-local database-wide distinct drug cardinality are
also available only as explicitly capped estimands. The latter uses a complete
public vocabulary-derived concept domain and canonical server-owned ordering:

```{r bounded-counts, eval=FALSE}
condition_records <- omop_querylibrary_sticky(
  "CO10", max_contributions = 25
)

distinct_rxnorm <- omop_querylibrary_sticky(
  "DEX06",
  variable = "drug_concept_id",
  levels = public_standard_rxnorm_ids,
  max_contributions = 50
)
```

For one server, DEX06 estimates the distinct cardinality across that site's
database. Across multiple servers there is no privacy-safe cross-site entity
linkage for computing a set union: `pool = TRUE` therefore returns the explicit
sum of site-local bounded distinct counts and may count a concept once per site.
Use `pool = FALSE` when site-specific cardinalities are the intended estimand;
do not interpret the pooled sum as a global union cardinality.

Exact ZIP, source/free-text labels and patient/event rows remain unavailable.
They do not silently fall back to a different query:

```{r blocked, error=TRUE}
omop_querylibrary_sticky("PE08")
```

Use `omop_querylibrary_sticky_catalog(include_unavailable = TRUE)` to inspect
the complete 201-ID partition: 129 executable bounded redesigns, 54
vocabulary/reference metadata questions, and 18 blocked result shapes.
